evidence.proposition: The normative dependency-direction rule and write footprints describe the Phase 1 renderer's authority over a previously installed lifecycle baseline.
evidence.failure_condition: A documented unconditional prohibition on rewriting a materialized baseline contradicts a successful upgrade replacement of a proven prior template.
evidence.public_path: render_platform_surfaces.py --repo-root <fixture> --platform codex --include-permissions --manifest <fixture manifest>, with and without the upgrade comparison checkpoint.

Inspect docs/architecture/domain-map.md rule 2, data-and-control-flow.md Path 3 State written and telemetry step 10 against Upgrade lifecycle baseline drift.
evidence.expected: Document the sole upgrade exception for the registered plan template and lifecycle prompts. Keep ordinary setup, unproven project files and the missing-only TechDocs trio outside that exception.
evidence.observed: The renderer left the prior templates intact without a checkpoint, then replaced six registered destinations after capturing the comparison. The public renderer retry also changed an existing prompt on both sides of CR-D1. Domain-map rule 2 states that a materialized baseline is never regenerated as a whole file. Path 3 says never rewritten afterwards, and telemetry step 10 says never replaced by a baseline. The dedicated upgrade section correctly describes replacement.

evidence.known_bad_detection_method: Compared the documented absolute prohibition with a real subprocess rewriting prior installed copies and the same subprocess preserving every copy with no captured checkpoint. A successful six-file replacement disproves the unconditional rule.
evidence.limitations: Fixtures run on macOS. Rehearsal evidence and fresh stdio inventories belong to the coordinator. This finding concerns architecture documentation. CR-D1 fixes a different fault during checkpoint publication.
evidence.safety_and_authorization: Only disposable local targets and host-settings fixtures were used.
evidence.disposition_rationale: Update the architecture authority and both stale restatements in the same change. Maintainers use rule 2 to decide whether modifying project-owned files is permitted.
